subject: How to handle this: Stan model for consumer choice data.

messages.author: 1c70f0703f55d650
messages.subject: How to handle this: Stan model for consumer choice data.
parts:
Hi,

I am seeking advice on how to implement the following hierarchical model in STAN.
Model description: consumers get individual level parameters (and error terms) from population level distributions and then choose quantities by maximizing utility. Using conditions for optimization, one is able to back out the implied error terms and form likelihood for quantity by change of variables. The likelihood for the data (quantity vectors of the type q=(q_1,..,q_m,0,...,0)) is fairly complex. 
We are attempting to recover all individual level parameters and the hyperparameters. 

I would really appreciate if you could give some pointers or answer the following questions:
1) how should I enter the "model part" in STAN for this kind of model? I have only seen examples where the probabilistic model for the data is very simple (a known distribution) like y~normal(theta,sigma).

2) Should HMCMC be done with block sampling or is it possible to sample all parameters (individual values and hyperparameters) in one iteration? What is the best practice?

I am actively learning and I would appreciate if you could point me to some references that deal with more complicated hierarchical models.
Thanks!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: How to handle this: Stan model for consumer choice data.
parts:
On Friday, November 4, 2016 at 5:06:57 PM UTC-4, Rudolf-Harri Oberg wrote:
I would really appreciate if you could give some pointers or answer the following questions:
1) how should I enter the "model part" in STAN for this kind of model? I have only seen examples where the probabilistic model for the data is very simple (a known distribution) like y~normal(theta,sigma).
We are trying to do a multinomial probit model in rstanarm. It is very difficult to sample effectively with such models and I can't say at this point it is working well enough.
2) Should HMCMC be done with block sampling or is it possible to sample all parameters (individual values and hyperparameters) in one iteration? What is the best practice?

Stan's implementation(s) of HMC only sample all parameters in one iteration, which is the best practice and is part of the main reason why Stan's implementation(s) of HMC work better than MCMC algorithms that block.

Ben

On Fri, Nov 4, 2016 at 5:06 PM, Rudolf-Harri Oberg <rudolf...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I am seeking advice on how to implement the following hierarchical model in STAN.
Model description: consumers get individual level parameters (and error terms) from population level distributions and then choose quantities by maximizing utility. Using conditions for optimization, one is able to back out the implied error terms and form likelihood for quantity by change of variables. The likelihood for the data (quantity vectors of the type q=(q_1,..,q_m,0,...,0)) is fairly complex. 
We are attempting to recover all individual level parameters and the hyperparameters. 

I would really appreciate if you could give some pointers or answer the following questions:
1) how should I enter the "model part" in STAN for this kind of model? I have only seen examples where the probabilistic model for the data is very simple (a known distribution) like y~normal(theta,sigma).

There are more complex models in the manual and on the example models: https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models

But... in general, all you have to do in the model block is compute the joint log probability distribution function of your data and parameters by using "target +=".
2) Should HMCMC be done with block sampling or is it possible to sample all parameters (individual values and hyperparameters) in one iteration? What is the best practice?
No need to specify this at all. Stan will perform MCMC over all the parameters jointly. The language doesn't have any specification of the algorithm.

I am actively learning and I would appreciate if you could point me to some references that deal with more complicated hierarchical models.
Thanks!
